questions.q: What is the official SI unit of time used by scientists around the world?
questions.a: The SI unit of time is the second (s). A wrong answer such as 'minute' or 'hour' reveals that the student confuses everyday convenient units of time with the internationally agreed-upon base SI unit.

questions.q: Trace the correct sequence from local timekeeping units to a single worldwide standard unit of time.
questions.a: The standardisation chain runs: (1) Traditional units like the ghati differ from region to region (2) Scientists need one common unit to share and compare measurements (3) The second is adopted as the SI base unit of time (4) Every speed and motion calculation worldwide uses the same consistent time unit. A wrong answer that claims traditional units serve science equally well shows the student has not understood why uniformity, consistency and unambiguous communication motivate the SI system.

questions.q: Convert a time interval of 3 hours and 15 minutes completely into seconds.
questions.a:
Step 1: Convert hours to minutes: $3 \text{ hours} \times 60 \text{ minutes/hour} = 180 \text{ minutes}$.
Step 2: Add the remaining minutes: $180 \text{ min} + 15 \text{ min} = 195 \text{ minutes}$.
Step 3: Convert total minutes to seconds: $195 \text{ min} \times 60 \text{ seconds/minute} = 11,700 \text{ seconds}$.
Answer: 11,700 s. A wrong answer reveals multiplication or unit conversion errors between minutes and seconds.

questions.q: Analyze what happens to the numerical value of a measured time interval if you change the unit from hours to seconds. Does the duration of the event itself change?
questions.a: The actual duration of the event does not change at all, but the numerical value becomes much larger because a second is a much smaller unit than an hour. A wrong answer indicates confusion between the physical quantity (duration) and the numerical scale used to measure it.

questions.q: Evaluate the following statement: "Since we use minutes to time our school periods and hours to measure a school day, the second is an unnecessary unit in physics." Is this correct? Explain.
questions.a: The statement is incorrect because physics formulas (like speed = distance / time) require a standard base unit for consistency across calculations. If different scientists used different units without a base SI unit, calculations would yield inconsistent and confusing results. A wrong answer shows a failure to appreciate the role of standard units in mathematical physics.

questions.q: Design a simple, low-cost investigation using your own pulse to estimate time intervals in seconds without looking at a wristwatch.
questions.a: A good response describes resting pulse rate (roughly 72 beats per minute, which is about 1.2 beats per second) and counting beats against a calibrated digital stopwatch to test consistency. A poor answer gives random guesses without a reference or calibration procedure.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: It measures the duration of events or intervals between ______.
Fill in the blank: Imagine listening to the steady tick-tock of a wall clock in your ______ or the beating of your own pulse after running in the school playground.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Can identify the second as the SI unit of time, convert time intervals between seconds, minutes, and hours accurately, and use seconds in standard physics calculations.
